## Clinical status

**General medical status:** Blood pressure: 120/70 mmHg supine, 125/71 mmHg standing. Pulse: 100/min supine, 125/min standing.

**Neurological status:** The patient is alert and oriented to time, place, self and surroundings. Attention is readily elicited, directed and sustained. Behaviour is appropriate to the examination setting. Mood is euthymic. The skull and spine are structurally normal and non-tender to percussion. The neck is supple, with no signs of meningeal irritation.

**Cranial nerves:** Visual acuity is preserved on gross examination; the patient wears sunglasses due to light sensitivity. Visual fields are full in both eyes on confrontation testing. The pupils are moderately dilated, equal, sharply demarcated, round and centrally positioned. Direct and consensual pupillary light responses are preserved. The palpebral fissures are equally wide. The eyes look straight ahead at rest, ocular movements are unrestricted in all directions, there is no nystagmus, and the patient reports no diplopia. The remaining cranial nerves are intact.

**Motor function:** Muscle bulk is appropriate to nutritional status, and muscle tone is normal throughout. Muscle strength is preserved throughout the limbs, and fine finger movements can be performed bilaterally. Tests for latent paresis are negative. Patellar reflexes are brisk and symmetrical in the lower limbs. There are no pyramidal signs. Superficial and deep sensation is preserved in the limbs and trunk. Abdominal cutaneous reflexes are elicitable bilaterally.

**Coordination:** There is no dysdiadochokinesia. The patient performs target-directed coordination tests accurately. The patient maintains stance in the Romberg position. Speech is fluent; comprehension, naming and repetition are intact. No release signs can be elicited. The patient has no urinary or faecal continence disturbance.

**Assessment:** Recommended investigations: laboratory tests, ECG, Mrtg, CDS, cranial CT.

## Imaging results

**ISMR MRI – 26 March 2025, 14:55**

**Cranial MRI, MRA and lumbar spine MRI examination – Stroke II.**

Sagittal 3D T1, axial T2-weighted, FLAIR, DWI and SWI sequences of the head were acquired.

This was followed by 3D TOF MRA and reconstructions of the major intracranial arteries at the base of the brain.

Sagittal T1- and T2-weighted, STIR, and sagittal and coronal MR myelographic sequences of the lumbar spine were acquired, followed by axial T2-weighted sequences at the L2–L5 intervertebral levels.

The supratentorial ventricular system is normally positioned and slightly asymmetrical, with the left lateral ventricle mildly larger. The fourth ventricle has a normal appearance. The subarachnoid cerebrospinal fluid spaces are preserved.

In the left frontal region, small, nonspecific subcortical foci of T2-FLAIR hyperintensity are observed; their clinical relevance is uncertain. No other abnormal intracranial signal, diffusion abnormality or evidence of haemorrhage is identified.

The midline is preserved. No space-occupying lesion is demonstrated.

The craniospinal junction is normal.

The intracranial arteries have a normal course and calibre, with signs of intact circulation. No aneurysm or abnormal vascular structure is identified on the images.

In the position examined, the lumbar lordosis is straightened, with no lateral curvature visible.

Impressions consistent with Schmorl's nodes are visible along the vertebral endplates, the most pronounced being at the inferior endplate of the L4 vertebra. A small area of oedematous signal abnormality is also visible in the surrounding region. Otherwise, vertebral alignment, height and signal intensity are normal. The facet joints are well aligned.

The L4/L5 intervertebral disc is dehydrated; otherwise, disc signal intensity and height are preserved. No disc herniation, nerve root compression or spinal canal stenosis is demonstrated. The conus medullaris terminates at the L1 vertebral level and has normal calibre and signal intensity.

**Impression:**

No pathological intracranial abnormality is demonstrated. Intact arterial system.

A Schmorl's node is demonstrated at the inferior endplate of the L4 vertebra, with oedematous signal abnormality. L4/L5 discopathy is observed. No disc herniation, nerve root compression or spinal canal stenosis is demonstrated.

## Discharge summary (epicrisis)

The patient was examined for symptoms persisting since May 2023 (possible brain fog, sensitivity to light and sound, and fatigability). The symptoms developed following repeated SARS-CoV-19 infection (the virus could not be detected). Interleukin levels measured through private testing were elevated. On admission, the neurological examination revealed no objective neurological signs; there was an increase in pulse rate suggestive of POTS.

Cranial MRI, MRA and lumbosacral spine MRI showed no abnormality explaining the patient's symptoms.

Routine laboratory testing showed mild lymphopenia. The antibody titre against the SARS-CoV-19 spike protein was high. As an objectively measurable parameter, repeat testing after three months is recommended (a referral has been provided).

Neurophysiological investigations (SSEP, BAEP, VEP, ENG, SSR) did not confirm a peripheral lesion.

In view of POTS, a specialist cardiology assessment is planned at our clinic to rule out organic pathology (the patient will be notified of the appointment and has been provided with a referral).

Persistent post-COVID syndrome is suspected to underlie the symptoms. No definitive aetiological treatment is available. Steroid treatment under close observation may be considered for symptomatic management. The patient has been informed and is considering this option for the time being. The patient is discharged home today.
